title: Clear Roadblocks Yourself

short.lead: A new rule would make me test every "I can't" claim, install missing tools myself, and never hand you a blocker I could clear; you pick how strongly it is enforced.
short.hint: Tap a step to see it.
items: Check the claim before making it

Before I say a tool, engine or machine is missing, I run the probe: which, ls, uname, hostname, or list_computer_folders. A claim made from memory is what went wrong on your PC: the session said Unity was absent and it was not on your PC, and neither was true.

items.alt: Flow from claim to probe to verdict
items.caption: The probe sits between the claim and the verdict.

items: Missing tool: install it, then carry on

In bypass permission mode I install anything missing (apt, pip, npm, a download) without asking, then re-run the step. In other modes the normal permission prompt is the ask. Only a purchase, a licence or a login is yours.
Nothing from you, except a licence or login.

If a route fails, I try the next one (another tool, an attached machine, a script, a different host) and list each attempt in the report. I stop only when every route is tried, and the report names them.

items.caption: A stop must list every route tried.

items: A line in the decisions log.
Pick an option, then send the approval line.

changes: The existing rule already says a "can't be done" claim needs a test. This extends it from claims to actions: a failed test is not the end, the next step is the fix.
Today: a claim needs a test; a Stop check flags "can't" with no tool run, and the users-hands rule says not to hand over labour.
New: a short section plus a detail file, Roadblocks are mine to clear, linked from both.
You stop being asked to install or switch machines.
Only in options B and C.
Flags replies that say "I can't", "not installed", "not on your machine", or "you need to install" when no probe or install ran this turn.
Today: the evidence check catches "can't" claims with no tool run at all.
New: it also catches the same claims after an unrelated tool ran, and "you need to install" hand-offs.
One block per reply, naming the probe to run.
choices: first
How firmly should this be enforced?
A
Rule text only: a new section and detail file, no hook change
Smallest; relies on me following it, and the session on your PC shows that is not enough.
B
Rule plus a Stop check that blocks roadblock claims with no probe (my suggestion)
Catches the exact failure, reuses the evidence-check machinery, and needs one verify.py case.
C
B plus a session-start line when in bypass mode saying installs are pre-approved
Strongest; adds text to every bypass session and depends on the hook being told the mode.
B closes the gap the rule alone leaves, without adding to every session's context.
second
What counts as yours, not mine?
A
Licences, logins, purchases and destructive actions only (my suggestion)
Matches the existing destructive-action and users-hands rules.
B
Also any install over a set size
Safer, but it brings back the stalls you asked me to stop.
Everything else is labour, which the rules already say is not yours.

wrapup.summary: This proposal adds a rule so I probe before claiming a blocker, install missing tools, and try other routes before stopping.
wrapup.changing: rules/house-rules.md, a new rules/detail/roadblocks.md, and in B or C the Stop check plus one verify.py case.
wrapup.blocking: Your pick of A, B or C, and your answer to what stays yours.
wrapup.next: After you approve, the work is planned in a build plan.
